comparisons.peer_topic: Benefit of government incentives on operating income
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, government incentives reduced expenses, benefiting operating income by $588 million, with approximately 85% allocated to COGS and 15% to R&D.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose that government incentives benefited operating income in fiscal 2024, with the majority of the benefit recorded in cost of sales (COGS). Intel reported a $442 million benefit, substantially majority in COGS, while Micron reported a $588 million benefit, with approximately 85% allocated to COGS. Both companies treat these incentives as a reduction of expense impacting operating income similarly.

sentences.text: Operating-related incentives, including those recognized under the CHIPS Act, benefited operating income by $442 million in 2024, the substantial majority of which was recorded in cost of sales ($202 million in 2023 and $104 million in 2022, a majority of which was recorded in cost of sales in both periods).
In 2024, operating income (loss) benefited by $588 million (approximately 85% in COGS and 15% in R&D) from government incentives recognized as a reduction of expense.

comparisons.peer_topic: CHIPS Act investment tax credit recognition
comparisons.peer_summary: Beginning in 2023, the company receives a 25% investment tax credit on qualified U.S. semiconductor manufacturing investments under the CHIPS Act, recognizing these credits in receivables or other noncurrent assets as investments are made.
comparisons.comparison: Intel explicitly mentions incentives recognized under the CHIPS Act as part of its operating-related incentives. Micron also details its receipt of a 25% investment tax credit on qualified U.S. semiconductor manufacturing investments specifically under the CHIPS Act beginning in 2023, confirming the same legislative source for the incentives discussed by Intel.
